layers.text: Style: bold chibi pixel art for a playful turn-based strategy board game, a board game come to life: chunky simple shapes, flat colours with one shadow tone, low detail, clean readable silhouette that reads at a glance at small size, slightly silly and cheerful.

layers.text: Camera: consistent strategy-game camera, three-quarter view looking slightly down, the subject faces down and to the right (south-east), whole subject visible and centred on a transparent background, nothing cropped. The subject stands directly on the empty transparent background: nothing at all is drawn under it.

Light: the sun is low in the south-west, at the bottom left of the image: faces turned to the left or to the viewer are lit, faces turned to the right are in shadow, snow is brightest on its left side, and nothing is lit from the right.

Class: one chunky cute creature map piece, a single living thing with big simple rounded rubbery shapes, big round eyes and a clear silhouette that reads at a glance, thick single-colour black outline; the whole creature is visible, and its lowest part is the lowest thing in the image. It holds no weapon and no tool.

layers.text: Subject: Thing in the Cellar, a chunky cute wide heap of a monster shown whole, a mound wider than it is tall: many fat rubbery deep-sea teal tentacles with pale cream suckers piled up and curling outward, many friendly round pale yellow eyes of different sizes with black pupils all over it, one round weathered grey-brown wooden trapdoor lid in its middle, one tiny striped party hat on top; no legs, no arms, no teeth; clearly a silly friendly monster, not scary; simple shapes and very few details.
The heap is drawn large and fills the whole square.
